title: Fomo Kernel Trade Premise
description: One hypothetical trade the model or user supplies mid-decision ('I'm thinking of buying NVDA — what does that do to my book?'). This is Layer 2 (docs/decision-fomo-kernel-shape.md §3): deterministic arithmetic over a premise, never a recommendation. The readable contract; skills/fomo-kernel/engine/consequence.py's validate_premise holds the enforcement, because the offline suite carries no jsonschema dependency. The envelope's field rules are stated once, here — consequence.py does not restate them, only enforces them. Also documents validate_premise's normalized OUTPUT shape (ticker/side/qty/price/price_basis/date/currency): every field the schema requires must be present on it, and it may carry no field the schema does not declare (tests/test_consequence.py's own structural-drift check) — price_basis is exactly such a field, engine-assigned and never caller-supplied (consequence._FIELDS excludes it from the input allowlist independently of this file).

ticker.description: The complete engine symbol, in the same form the ledger's own rows use (for example NVDA, 2330.TW). Matching the ledger's convention is what lets before/after states compare the same instrument rather than two strings that merely look alike.

side.description: Which direction the hypothetical trade goes. A sell is checked against what is currently held (a sell of an unheld ticker, or more shares than are held, is refused rather than silently clamped or read as a short) because this layer computes consequences of a real position change, not a speculative short thesis.

price.description: The hypothetical execution price, in the instrument's own trading currency. Optional (#777, owner ruling 2026-08-02): when the caller states no price, consequence.validate_premise defaults it to the engine's own observed close for this ticker (the same last_px map every other number in the answer is priced from) rather than asking for one or refusing outright, and stamps price_basis 'observed' so the two remain distinguishable downstream. Refused, naming the ticker, when neither a stated price nor an observed one is available -- a premise this engine cannot price is still never answered on an invented number. When notional is given instead of qty, this is also what notional divides through to become a share count -- the stated or the defaulted value, either way -- because the engine's downstream arithmetic is share-based, matching how the ledger itself is recorded.

price_basis.description: Engine-assigned, never a field the caller may send (consequence._FIELDS does not include it, independently of this schema's own additionalProperties:false). Present only on validate_premise's normalized OUTPUT and therefore on a stored trade-evaluation row's premise, never on the input envelope a caller constructs. 'user_stated' when the caller supplied price; 'observed' when it was left out and the engine filled it from its own observed close -- the fact evaluation_challenge.py's must_state now states under the position topic whenever it is 'observed', so 'priced at the last close' reaches the user rather than reading as an ordinary chosen price.

qty.description: Hypothetical share count. Mutually exclusive with notional (oneOf below) — the caller states the trade the one way they actually have it in mind, and the engine derives the other, rather than both being supplied and silently disagreeing.

notional.description: Hypothetical trade size in cash terms (this instrument's currency). Converted to qty via notional / price. Mutually exclusive with qty.

date.description: When the hypothetical trade would happen. Optional — defaults to the day after the ledger's last row, so an unstated premise reads as 'if I did this next' rather than silently backdating into history. A date earlier than the last ledger row is refused: this layer computes a forward consequence, not a rewrite of what already happened.

currency.description: Trading currency of the price. Optional — defaults to the ticker's own currency in the ledger when it is already held, or USD for a new position, so an omitted currency cannot silently mis-aggregate a mixed-currency book.
